name: Right-libertarianism
summary: Right-libertarianism holds that individuals fully own themselves and may acquire unowned resources by first use or labor, so that capitalist property rights and free markets are just and taxation and redistribution are rights violations. Governments should be abolished (anarcho-capitalists) or confined to a night-watchman role of courts, police and defense (minarchists). Most adherents favor legal drugs and sex work, non-interventionism abroad and an end to the welfare state, while splitting on immigration, abortion and cultural questions.
scope: The Rothbard-Nozick core as set out in Rothbard's For a New Liberty and Man, Economy, and State and in the SEP and IEP: self-ownership, homesteading, the non-aggression principle, with the minimal-state (Nozick) and anarcho-capitalist (Rothbard) wings both counted, and an answer of 0 where they disagree. Left-libertarianism (common ownership of resources) is excluded.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 9) says the money supply should come from a free market, as gold and silver did, in place of the government's fiat paper standard and its central banking.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 1) praises the classical liberals' abolition of the feudal privileges of entail and primogeniture and opposes hereditary hierarchy.

abolish-income-tax.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 12 and 15) says repeal of the income tax would force government back to minor levels of power and prefers abolishing income taxation to small cuts.

abortion-legal.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 6) rests on the absolute right of every woman to own her own body and concludes that the fetus has no right to remain unbidden in it.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 2) bases land ownership on homesteading by individuals and rejects communal or state ownership.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 1) lists religious freedom and the separation of Church and State among the liberal goals conservatism opposed, and (ch. 6) defines a crime as only the violent invasion of another's person or property.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 14) says the United States should stop its incessant political meddling abroad and abolish the CIA.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 9) attacks Keynesian economics and its approval of government spending of every kind as inflationary and wasteful.

ban-cartels.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 2) lists antitrust laws among the government interventions that violate the principle of liberty.

basic-income.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 8) rejects the guaranteed annual income and negative income tax and calls instead for abolition of the welfare dole.

bound-labor.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 5, Involuntary Servitude) condemns forced labor and holds that every person owns himself; he credits classical liberals with abolishing feudal bonds and privileges.

build-apartments-freely.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 8) blames zoning laws for ringing housing and land use with restrictions that cripple urban development.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 14) blames war on the State and its standing armies, and associates peace with free trade and the market.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 6) names pornography among the victimless acts and the freedom to speak and publish among the civil liberties libertarians defend.

central-planning.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 10) says central planning under socialism is deprived of accurate pricing and so cannot calculate costs and prices, which is why it has failed.

civilians-legitimate-targets.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 1) says modern war entails mass slaughter of civilians, which makes it mass murder and totally illegitimate.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 1) condemns imperialism, including the 'Liberal Imperialism' of later liberals, and traces opposition to it to laissez-faire liberals.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 1) condemns imperialism as state aggrandizement and mercantilism for the gain of privileged merchants.

conscription.rationale: Rothbard states that conscription is slavery on a massive scale (ch. 1 and 5); the IEP lists conscription among rights-violating state acts.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 1 and 9) condemns the corporatist state that made trade unions junior partners of government and rejects state-conferred union privileges.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 6) says sexual deviation is not a crime, since a crime is only a violent invasion of another's person or property.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 7 and 8) says a 'right' to meals or a job is not natural and calls for abolishing the welfare system.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 6) argues that 'protective' labor laws for women discriminate against them and should be repealed.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 7 and 8) says a 'right' to meals or a job is not natural, since it would require coercing others, and he calls for abolishing the welfare dole.

distribution-by-process.rationale: The SEP and IEP describe Nozick's historical entitlement theory, on which a distribution is just if it arose by just acquisition and transfer, whatever its pattern.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 14) calls for total withdrawal from abroad and strict political neutrality, which leaves no room for permanent alliances.

foreign-policy-non-interference.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 14) makes withdrawal from everywhere and strict political neutrality the primary plank of a libertarian foreign policy.

free-trade-promotes-peace.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 1) credits the classical liberals with a foreign policy of peace and free trade with all nations.

gradual-change.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 15) rejects gradualism as a strategy and says libertarians should demand abolition of statism as quickly as possible, as the abolitionists did with slavery.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 2) holds that the homesteader who first puts unused land to use acquires it, and the SEP describes right-libertarianism as allowing appropriation by first use or labour.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 2) says rights are those of each individual, and the IEP says libertarians hold individuals, not groups, to be normatively primary.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 14) rejects American intervention abroad in all forms.

job-guarantee.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 7) says a 'right' to a job or meals is not part of man's nature, since it can only be supplied by coercing others.

land-redistribution.rationale: The SEP says right-libertarians allow appropriation by first use without regard to the pattern of distribution, and Rothbard (ch. 2) holds property earned by homesteading or exchange to be inviolable.

land-value-tax.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 2) rejects Henry George's denial of individual ownership of land itself, and holds all taxation to be robbery.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 1) faults conservatism for replacing religious freedom with the theocratic rule of a State church, and (ch. 6) defines a crime as only the violent invasion of another's person or property.

legal-duty-to-work.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 5, Involuntary Servitude) opposes compulsory labor and says labor should be free; he rejects forcing welfare recipients to work as a fraud.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Rothbard names drug laws among the 'victimless crimes' libertarians would repeal, since a crime is only a violent invasion of person or property (ch. 6); the IEP lists drug bans as rights-violating.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Rothbard says prostitution is a voluntary sale of a labor service that the government has no right to prohibit or restrict (ch. 6).

limit-growth.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 13) calls the cry for cessation of growth truly obscene while much of the world lives in squalor, and defends growth under property rights.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Rothbard's chapters on government in business, roads, police and money argue that the voluntary market serves consumers better than government provision, and the IEP names markets and economic liberty as part of the libertarian core.

military-force-beyond-defence.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 14) rejects American intervention abroad and wants force used, if at all, only to defend persons and property.

military-force-for-human-rights.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 14) says the United States should abandon global interventionism and withdraw militarily and politically from everywhere.

money-backed-by-precious-metals.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 9) argues that gold and silver won out as money on the market, and contrasts that with the government's fiat paper standard.

national-mission.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 14) calls for the United States to abandon global interventionism and political meddling everywhere.

natural-rulers.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 1) says conservatism's hierarchical rule by privileged elites replaced equal rights and equality before the law, which he defends.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 8) rejects the negative income tax and guaranteed annual income as no genuine replacement for the welfare system.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The IEP describes Nozick's minimal state limited to police, courts and military, while anarcho-capitalists such as Rothbard say even that state is too large and should be abolished; the strands split on this.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 1, 10 and 11) repeatedly condemns special privileges, subsidies and monopoly grants that governments give to favoured businesses.

no-central-bank.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 9) condemns the Federal Reserve System's control of the money supply and argues for money that emerges from the free market.

party-controls-media.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 6 and 10) criticises the government's grip on radio and television channels as incompatible with freedom of speech.

positive-liberty.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 7) says a 'right' to schooling, jobs or meals is not part of man's nature, since it can only be supplied by coercing others.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 9) wants price and wage controls abolished at once.

price-controls-fight-inflation.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 9) wants price and wage controls abolished and blames inflation on the government's money creation.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 12) argues that courts and police can be supplied by competing private firms; the minimal-state strand following Nozick keeps courts as a function of the state (IEP).

promote-democracy-abroad.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 14) calls for ending political meddling in other countries.

property-fundamental.rationale: The IEP lists robust property rights among the libertarian cluster of principles, and Rothbard (ch. 2) makes the right to person and property the basis of his system.

public-ownership.rationale: Chapter 10 of For a New Liberty (Government in Business) argues that government-run enterprises should be returned to private owners.

public-service-media.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 6 and 10) criticises government ownership and licensing of broadcasting and holds that such activity should be private.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 1) lists religious freedom and the separation of Church and State among the liberal goals conservatism opposed, and (ch. 6) defines a crime as only the violent invasion of another's person or property.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Rothbard (For a New Liberty, ch. 8) says minimum wage laws generate unemployment among the poorest and least skilled, and calls for none.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Rothbard treats government regulation and compulsory cartelization of business as the tools of the statist 'New Right' and corporate liberalism (ch. 1 and 10), not as a remedy.

rent-control.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 8) says rent controls created apartment shortages and reduced the housing supply.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: The SEP says right-libertarianism lets resources be appropriated by first use without any payment to others, in contrast to left-libertarianism, which requires a payment for the value of appropriated resources.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 1) lists religious freedom and the separation of Church and State among the liberal goals conservatism opposed, and (ch. 6) defines a crime as only the violent invasion of another's person or property.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Rothbard says the libertarian stands for the freedom to speak, publish and assemble (ch. 6); a legal ban on a kind of speech is the opposite.

restrict-private-adult-pornography-acces.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 6) names pornography among the victimless crimes that are not crimes at all.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 10) says the remedy for union disruption is not to pass laws outlawing strikes but to remove the special legal privileges unions hold.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 14) says the United States should end all foreign aid, which coerces taxpayers to subsidize favoured foreign states.

school-vouchers.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 7) calls Friedman's voucher plan an improvement on public schools but says the libertarian still objects to coerced subsidy and the regulation that comes with it.

self-ownership.rationale: Self-ownership is the core right of the doctrine: Rothbard (ch. 2) makes each person's ownership of his own body the foundation, and the SEP says both left and right libertarians agree on it.

separate-church-state.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 1) presents the separation of Church and State as part of the classical-liberal tradition he continues, with religion set free from state imposition or interference.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 12) says that exempting the authorities from the criminal law that binds everyone else gives them a licence to commit aggression.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 3) treats the state as a coercive apparatus run by a parasitic ruling group living off the rest of society; the SEP notes this view of the state as a class vehicle in the individualist anarchist tradition he draws on.

state-harmful.rationale: Anarcho-capitalists such as Rothbard hold that no state is justified, while Nozick and other minimal-state libertarians hold that a state limited to police, courts and the military is legitimate (IEP); both strands are within the scope.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 14) calls for the United States to withdraw totally within its own boundaries and keep strict neutrality everywhere.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Rothbard calls wiretapping a contemptible invasion of privacy and property that should be outlawed, even though it may catch criminals (ch. 12).

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 1) lists the protective tariff and mercantilist restrictions among the statist measures, and praises the classical liberal foreign policy of free trade with all nations.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Rothbard holds taxation to be robbery (ch. 1 and 15) and the right to property to include the right to give it away.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Rothbard holds all taxation to be robbery (For a New Liberty, ch. 1 and 15), so a heavier tax on one group is a larger theft, not a fairer share.

taxation-theft.rationale: Rothbard states that taxation is robbery, a forcible taking by the state (ch. 1 and 2).

territorial-expansion.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 1 and 14) condemns imperialism and the war-making nation-state.

total-state.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 1) holds up the separation of the economy, speech and religion from the State, so a state directing every area of life is the opposite.

trade-surplus.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 1) condemns mercantilism and its restrictions on trade as the work of the war-making state and privileged merchants.

troops-home-from-abroad.rationale: Rothbard (ch. 14) says the United States should dismantle its bases and withdraw its troops everywhere.

missingStatements.text: Whether a distribution of wealth is just depends on how it came about, not on how equal it is.
missingStatements.rationale: The SEP states that right-libertarian distributive justice is historical, so redistribution is justified only to correct wrongful takings.
